question: At one point the frozen round-4 binary you were comparing against printed no benchmark line at all. What was the cause?
answer:
Cause: the frozen round-4 binary could not find its Metal sources, so shader compilation failed at startup and it never dispatched a frame — hence no benchmark line at all.

Details: the program compiles its kernels at runtime with newLibraryWithSource by reading the shaders directory next to the executable. When I froze round 4 into the A/B base directory (ab_r4/), I copied the tree with `cp -R pathtracer/include ab_r4/` style commands; because the destination directory already existed, cp nested the contents one level down (include/include, shaders/shaders). The binary itself launched fine and printed nothing wrong except the missing 'render_ms_best=...' line, since the shader-source load failed silently and the run produced no frames.

How I know: this is recorded in my round-5 working memory entry 'round5-refs' (evidence messages 75-86), where I noted the cp -R nesting bug produced nested include/include and a silent shader-compile failure of the base, and the standing rule I derived from it — always verify the A/B base binary actually prints a benchmark line before trusting a comparison. I confirmed it by listing the copy and seeing the doubled directory level, then re-copied the headers and shaders flat next to the binary, after which it printed its benchmark line normally.

question: At one point the frozen round-4 binary you were comparing against printed no benchmark line at all. What was the cause?
answer:
Cause: the frozen round-4 binary never got its Metal sources, so it failed at shader compile time and exited before ever dispatching a frame — the harness then had no 'render_ms_best=...' line to parse and silently recorded nothing for the base.

Details: the program compiles its kernels at startup with MTLDevice newLibraryWithSource, reading the .metal files from a `shaders` directory located next to the executable. When I froze round 4 into the A/B directory (ab_r4/) I copied the tree with `cp -R pathtracer/include ab_r4/include` while `ab_r4/include` already existed, so cp nested the payload one level deeper (ab_r4/include/include/..., same for shaders). The binary was therefore sitting next to an empty-looking layout and found no shaders; newLibraryWithSource returned nil, the host reported the compile failure on stderr and returned non-zero, and my _ab.sh wrapper (which only greps the last stdout line and skips empty results) dropped those rounds without complaining. That is why the base printed no benchmark line at all, and why I added the rule to my working memory: after freezing a base, always confirm it actually prints a benchmark line before trusting any A/B numbers.

How I know: it is recorded in my round-5 working-memory entry 'round5-refs' (evidence messages 75-86), which notes the cp -R nesting produced nested include/include and a silent shader-compile failure of the base; the fix was to copy include/ and shaders/ flat next to the frozen binary and re-verify the base emitted a timing line.
